note.note:
Consult Summary:
35-year-old male reports 3–6 months of reduced appetite, weight loss (~1 stone), low energy and episodic palpitations/shortness of breath in lifts. History of untreated hypothyroidism; blood tests arranged to investigate fatigue, weight loss and cardiovascular symptoms.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Fatigue, anorexia and unintentional weight loss
- Loss of appetite and energy for ~3.5 months, coinciding with job change.
- Weight loss ≈1 stone over ~6 months.
- Associated symptoms: intermittent nausea without vomiting, no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool, no reflux.
- No exertional dyspnoea; able to walk a mile without breathlessness (when active).
- Differential: anaemia, uncontrolled hypothyroidism (off thyroxine), vitamin deficiencies, mood disorder, malignancy (less likely but to be ruled out).

Issue 2: Palpitations / episodic shortness of breath
- Episodes occur primarily in lifts; patient feels heart racing and difficulty breathing.
- No chest pain, no cough, no exertional dyspnoea on walking.
- Advised to seek urgent care if chest pain or persistent palpitations develop.
- Differential: anxiety/panic, thyroid dysfunction, arrhythmia.

Issue 3: History of underactive thyroid – medication non-adherence
- Previously on thyroxine; stopped “since I changed doctor” (exact duration unclear).
- No recent thyroid function tests.
- Possible link to current symptoms.

Medications:
- Thyroxine (levothyroxine) – dose/route/frequency not documented; currently not taking.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer.
- Married; wife notes decreased libido/nightly activity.
- Physical activity low; “haven’t been walking lately.”
- Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No information provided regarding cancer screening, vaccinations, or other preventive care.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth consultation; no examination performed.
- Vitals not recorded.

Plan:
- Order comprehensive blood work: FBC, renal profile, liver profile, thyroid function tests, vitamin B12, folate, iron studies ± ferritin, and any other baseline profiles per local protocol.
- Patient to phone support number (provided via app) to arrange phlebotomy.
- Results to be reviewed; patient will receive text to book follow-up. 
- If bloods normal, schedule in-person physical examination.
- Red-flag advice: attend A&E for chest pain, sustained palpitations, new vomiting, or altered bowel habits.
- Consider restarting or adjusting thyroxine pending TFT results.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: allergies, current medication reconciliation (other than thyroxine), family history, mental health screening, vitals, smoking/alcohol status.
● No internal content conflicts noted.
● Transcript quality: occasional inaudible/over-talk but main clinical content clear.
